# Bath and North East Somerset - council briefing

*Auto-generated from council minutes, 30 April 2026 to 13 August 2026*

## What's dominating the agenda

Transport & Highways leads with 2,937 keyword hits, mostly through Cabinet and the Planning Committee, closely followed by Children & Education (2,897, split between Cabinet and the Children, Adults, Health and Wellbeing Policy Development and Scrutiny Panel) and Climate & Environment (2,896, largely Planning Committee casework and the Climate Emergency and Sustainability Panel).

## Notable decisions

- Cabinet adopted the Movement Strategy for Bath, following a public consultation and revisions made in response to feedback (key decision, 2 Jul).
- The Cabinet Member for Sustainable Transport Delivery approved an extra £0.92m for the CRSTS Manvers Street Remediation capital programme (key decision, approved, 4 Jun).
- Cabinet retrospectively approved the Local SEND Reform Plan, aimed at strengthening inclusion in mainstream schools and improving outcomes for children and young people (key decision, 2 Jul).
- Cabinet delegated approval of funding and infrastructure agreements to deliver affordable homes on the Bath Western Riverside Phase 2 site (key decision, 2 Jul).
- The Cabinet Member for Resources approved a Crisis and Resilience Fund allocation, which includes withdrawing Free School Meal vouchers after 2026 (key decision, approved, 11 May).
- The Cabinet Member for Communications and Community introduced a Public Spaces Protection Order in council-owned cemeteries to tackle dog fouling and control (key decision, 24 Jun).

## Worth a closer look

- The Audit Committee received the external auditor's plan for the year ending 31 March 2026 (13 May). [source](https://councilgateway.poteris.co.uk/council-api/documents/1429464/file)
- The Health and Wellbeing Board considered the new Bath and North East Somerset Food Strategy, covering 2026 to 2031 (7 May). [source](https://councilgateway.poteris.co.uk/council-api/documents/1423715/file)
- Planning Committee decided a Regulation 3 application for the former Post Office premises on Northgate Street in Bath city centre (13 May). [source](https://councilgateway.poteris.co.uk/council-api/documents/1449079/file)
- The Licensing Sub-Committee considered a premises licence application for High Acres in Tunley, Bathavon South (30 Apr). [source](https://councilgateway.poteris.co.uk/council-api/documents/1417892/file)

## Projects on residents' radar

- **Bath Quays North** - the Cabinet Member for Finance and Resources signed off extra funding within the existing Bath Quays North capital budget to cover site development costs run up by the council's development partner, Aequus Construction (27 Jul). [source](https://democracy.bathnes.gov.uk/ieDecisionDetails.aspx?ID=2480)
- **Somer Valley Links** - a temporary £1.27m budget was approved to keep the WECA-funded Somer Valley Links transport scheme on track for a 2026 construction start while a permanent funding uplift is agreed (21 May). [source](https://democracy.bathnes.gov.uk/ieDecisionDetails.aspx?ID=2440)
- **Somer Valley Design Code** - Cabinet adopted a design code setting standards for new housing across Midsomer Norton, Paulton, Peasedown, Radstock and Westfield (16 May). [source](https://democracy.bathnes.gov.uk/ieDecisionDetails.aspx?ID=2439)
- **Winifred's Lane, Catharine Place and Gay Street trial schemes** - after six months of public consultation, the council made these Bath city-centre traffic trials permanent (30 Jan). [source](https://democracy.bathnes.gov.uk/ieDecisionDetails.aspx?ID=2378)
- **Scholars Way** - the council accepted just under £3m of West of England Combined Authority funding to start construction of the Scholars Way scheme (26 Jan). [source](https://democracy.bathnes.gov.uk/ieDecisionDetails.aspx?ID=2377)
